sections.title: Raised cups and the harvest underfoot
sections.bodyMarkdown:
Three figures gather in long dresses of pale, red and warm yellow tones, raising golden cups overhead. The central figure has their back to the viewer, turns towards the others and lifts one foot. The figures to either side direct their eyes and arms towards the group. Flowing fabric and overlapping movements make the scene lively.

Grapes, leaves, orange gourds and other plants lie on the ground. The figure on the right holds a bunch of grapes in the other hand, against an open blue sky. Cups come together above a harvest at their feet. The picture shows shared celebration; it does not depict someone being excluded or a secret affair. [View the card image](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Cups03.jpg)

sections.title: Historical meanings of fulfilment and excess
sections.bodyMarkdown:
The 1911 English transcription of Waite’s The Pictorial Key to the Tarot describes figures raising cups in a garden. Upright meanings concern a plentiful conclusion, joy, fulfilment and consolation. Alongside completion and dispatch, the reversed entry explicitly includes excessive sensual enjoyment. [Waite’s entry for this card](https://original.sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pktcu03.htm)

This site uses those themes to discuss celebration and social support. Extending the reversal to social exhaustion and group pressure is a modern line of inquiry. The historical language of healing is not a medical conclusion, and a gathering is not a remedy for every difficulty.

sections.title: Upright: Let achievements be more than finished tasks
sections.bodyMarkdown:
The card can remind you to recognise completion. A team delivers a project; a friend gets through a demanding period. Either can deserve a pause to celebrate. You do not have to wait until every problem disappears before allowing happiness.

Good support does not require constant agreement. It allows honest congratulations, practical help and people moving at different paces. Thank people for particular contributions so they know their effort has actually been seen.

sections.title: Reversed: Notice when participation becomes a burden
sections.bodyMarkdown:
Back-to-back engagements, spending beyond your budget to fit in, or leaving the same person to clean up every time can make enjoyable company feel heavy. The reversal invites a look at frequency, cost and shared labour; you may not need to leave the entire friendship group.

Another possibility is that celebration never happens because nothing feels good enough, or acknowledging success feels boastful. Keep it small: share an update with one or two trusted people instead of forcing yourself into a lively gathering.

sections.title: Make support more specific
sections.bodyMarkdown:
At the end of a project, hold a short review, thank those who actually carried the work and give quieter teammates a way to contribute in writing. A celebration should not replace unresolved discussion about responsibilities.

For a friend’s birthday meal, check the budget and dietary preferences in advance, and make room for people who do not drink or want to leave early. When joining an interest group, notice whether beginners are welcome, rather than judging only by cheerful photographs.

sections.title: Practice: Plan a light-touch celebration
sections.bodyMarkdown: Write down one recent achievement and two people who supported it. Choose a low-pressure way to thank them: a specific message, a walk together or sharing the finished work. Check whether it suits them first, so gratitude does not turn into compulsory attendance.

sections.bodyMarkdown: Three figures in a picture do not imply a third party in a real relationship, and a reversal cannot prove betrayal. If exclusivity concerns you, discuss agreed boundaries and actual behaviour. Turning the number of figures directly into an accusation skips the evidence that matters.

articleMarkdown:
# Three of Cups Meaning: Give joy someone to share it with

In one sentence: When something goes well, acknowledge the joy with the people who supported you.

Card: Three of Cups  
Rank: III · RWS Minor Arcana · Cups  
Keywords: Celebration · Friendship · Group support

Upright at a glance: Gather with people who support one another, and name the achievement and your thanks.  
Reversed at a glance: Socialising or obligations may be draining you. Adjust how much and how you take part.

Some joys are enough simply to know for yourself. Others gain another layer when shared with the people who were there along the way. The Three of Cups brings that group into view.

## Raised cups and the harvest underfoot

Three figures gather in long dresses of pale, red and warm yellow tones, raising golden cups overhead. The central figure has their back to the viewer, turns towards the others and lifts one foot. The figures to either side direct their eyes and arms towards the group. Flowing fabric and overlapping movements make the scene lively.

Grapes, leaves, orange gourds and other plants lie on the ground. The figure on the right holds a bunch of grapes in the other hand, against an open blue sky. Cups come together above a harvest at their feet. The picture shows shared celebration; it does not depict someone being excluded or a secret affair. [View the card image](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Cups03.jpg)

## Historical meanings of fulfilment and excess

The 1911 English transcription of Waite’s The Pictorial Key to the Tarot describes figures raising cups in a garden. Upright meanings concern a plentiful conclusion, joy, fulfilment and consolation. Alongside completion and dispatch, the reversed entry explicitly includes excessive sensual enjoyment. [Waite’s entry for this card](https://original.sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pktcu03.htm)

This site uses those themes to discuss celebration and social support. Extending the reversal to social exhaustion and group pressure is a modern line of inquiry. The historical language of healing is not a medical conclusion, and a gathering is not a remedy for every difficulty.

## Upright: Let achievements be more than finished tasks

The card can remind you to recognise completion. A team delivers a project; a friend gets through a demanding period. Either can deserve a pause to celebrate. You do not have to wait until every problem disappears before allowing happiness.

Good support does not require constant agreement. It allows honest congratulations, practical help and people moving at different paces. Thank people for particular contributions so they know their effort has actually been seen.

## Reversed: Notice when participation becomes a burden

Back-to-back engagements, spending beyond your budget to fit in, or leaving the same person to clean up every time can make enjoyable company feel heavy. The reversal invites a look at frequency, cost and shared labour; you may not need to leave the entire friendship group.

Another possibility is that celebration never happens because nothing feels good enough, or acknowledging success feels boastful. Keep it small: share an update with one or two trusted people instead of forcing yourself into a lively gathering.

## Make support more specific

At the end of a project, hold a short review, thank those who actually carried the work and give quieter teammates a way to contribute in writing. A celebration should not replace unresolved discussion about responsibilities.

For a friend’s birthday meal, check the budget and dietary preferences in advance, and make room for people who do not drink or want to leave early. When joining an interest group, notice whether beginners are welcome, rather than judging only by cheerful photographs.

## Practice: Plan a light-touch celebration

Write down one recent achievement and two people who supported it. Choose a low-pressure way to thank them: a specific message, a walk together or sharing the finished work. Check whether it suits them first, so gratitude does not turn into compulsory attendance.

## A common misreading

Three figures in a picture do not imply a third party in a real relationship, and a reversal cannot prove betrayal. If exclusivity concerns you, discuss agreed boundaries and actual behaviour. Turning the number of figures directly into an accusation skips the evidence that matters.

## Read alongside

Two of Cups: Compare a two-person exchange with being part of a group; Ten of Cups: Move from a single celebration to maintaining lasting belonging.

sourceRecord.oneLineSummary: 一件事做成了，与支持你的人一起承认这份喜悦。
sourceRecord.uprightQuickTake: 和能彼此支持的人相聚，把成果与感谢说出来。
sourceRecord.reversedQuickTake: 聚会或人情开始耗人，调整参与方式与分寸。
sourceRecord.hook: 有些高兴，自己知道就很好；有些高兴，说给一起走过来的人听，会多一层分量。圣杯三把视线带到这群人中间。

sections.title: 举杯的人与脚下的收获
paragraphs: 三个人围在一起，分别穿浅色、红色和暖黄色的长裙，金杯举向头顶。中间人物背对观者，身体转向同伴，一只脚抬起；左右人物的视线与手臂也向圈内聚拢。衣褶与交错动作让场景显得活跃。
地面有葡萄、叶片、橙色瓜果等植物，右边人物另一只手提着一串葡萄，背景是开阔蓝天。杯子在上方相聚，收获铺在脚边；这幅画呈现共同庆贺的姿态，没有画出谁被排除在外，也没有显示秘密恋情。 [查看本篇牌面](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Cups03.jpg)

sections.title: 丰盛结局与过度享乐的旧义
paragraphs: Waite《塔罗图解之钥》1911 英文转录把场景写成园地中举杯致意的人，正位词条涉及丰盛的结束、欢乐、实现与慰藉。逆位除了完成、处理等词，也明确提到感官享受过量的一面。 [Waite 本牌原文](https://original.sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pktcu03.htm)
本站借此讨论庆祝与人际支持；把逆位延伸为社交消耗、群体压力，是面向现代生活的提问。原文的疗愈用语不构成医学结论，聚会也不是解决所有难受的办法。

sections.title: 正位 别让成果只剩下待办清单
paragraphs: 这张牌可以提醒你，完成值得被认出来。团队交出一个项目，朋友熬过一段忙碌时期，都可以停下来庆祝；不必等所有问题消失，才允许自己开心。
有质量的支持不是每个人永远赞同，而是能诚实祝贺、愿意帮忙，也容得下不同步的人。把感谢说到具体贡献，大家才知道自己的努力确实被看见。

sections.title: 逆位 看参与有没有变成负担
paragraphs: 连续应酬、为了合群超出预算、每次聚餐都由同一个人收尾，都会让原本愉快的交往变沉重。逆位可以用来检查频率、费用与劳动分配，未必需要退出整个朋友圈。
另一个方向是庆祝迟迟不能发生：总觉得还不够好，或者怕承认成果会显得自满。此时可以把聚会做小，只与一两位信任的人分享近况，而不强迫自己热闹。

sections.title: 怎样让支持更具体
paragraphs: 工作收尾后，开一场短复盘，点名感谢实际承担任务的人，也让不爱发言的同伴有书面表达的机会。不要用庆功代替未解决的分工问题。
朋友生日聚餐，先确认预算和饮食偏好，让不喝酒或想早走的人自在参与。加入兴趣小组时，观察群体能否接纳初学者，而不仅看照片里是否气氛很好。

sections.title: 练习 设计一次轻量庆祝
paragraphs: 写下一件最近已经完成的事，以及两位提供过支持的人。挑一种彼此负担小的方式表达感谢：一条具体的消息、一起散步或分享成果。先确认对方是否方便，不把感谢变成必须出席的邀请。

sections.title: 容易看错的地方
paragraphs: 画中三个人不等于现实中的第三者，逆位也不能证明某人背叛。若担心关系排他性，应当讨论已经约定的边界和实际行为。把人数直接翻译成指控，会跳过最重要的证据。
